extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the Ford Foundation Fellowships (graduate students and early-career scholars pursuing academic faculty careers)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and selection standards for the Ford Foundation Fellowships, a program intended to increase faculty diversity by supporting individuals at multiple stages of academic careers. Guidance centers on applicant qualities (academic achievement, career commitment, promise) and use of diversity as a pedagogical resource, plus program supports (mentorship, professional development, alumni network).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose — increase faculty diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ford Foundation Fellowships were designed to increase the diversity of the nation's college and university faculties by increasing their ethnic and racial diversity, maximizing the educational benefits of diversity, and increasing the number of professors who use diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program addressed these goals through a series of fellowships that spanned multiple stages of an academic career as well as mentorship, professional development, and an expansive network of alumni who enable peer support and community building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior academic achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for individuals who demonstrated superior academic achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a primary criterion for selection; applicants are expected to show evidence of high academic accomplishment (no detailed scoring rubric provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to a career in teaching and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have committed to a career in teaching and research at the college or university level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment implies intention to pursue faculty positions and sustained engagement in both teaching and scholarly research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should have shown promise of future achievement as scholars and teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators would consider indicators of future potential (research trajectory, teaching potential, recommendations), though the page does not provide detailed evidentiary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diversity as a resource for enriching student education
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should have used diversity as a resource for enriching the education of all students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion emphasizes demonstrated practice or plans that leverage ethnic, racial, or other forms of diversity to improve teaching and learning; examples or evidence are not listed on this page but would likely include pedagogical approaches, mentorship, curriculum development, or outreach activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship scope — multiple academic career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ford fellowships spanned multiple stages of an academic career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program provided different fellowship types across career stages (implied by the description); applicants should consult specific RFA or program materials for stage-specific eligibility and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program supports — mentorship, professional development, alumni network
rubrics_metrics.description: Ford Foundational Fellows received mentorship, professional development, and an expansive alumni network to enable peer support and community building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the award itself, the fellowship offered facilitated engagement with an alumni community and ongoing professional-development resources to support career advancement and networking.
